messages.author: 628053524651bedc
messages.subject: Scaling for measurement items
parts:
Hello,

I have used 7 point scales for most of my measurements.
On one latent construct, I have three items 
a) 7 point scale (EX01)
b) ruler with 101 steps (EX02)
c) 3 point scale (EX03) (closer to binary)

All three can potentially reflect one construct.

If I use the following statement in the measurement model. 
Use =~ EX01 + EX02 + EX03

I get the following warning:
Warning message: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster, : lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate

I did run the varTable() and found that the the variance in EX02
EX01 mean  2.414   var 3.702  
EX02 mean  32.940 var 1065.488
EX03 mean 1.750    var 0.903

Is there a good way to scale EX02 or all 3 to work around the variance issue?


Thanks for all replies !

Carsten

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Scaling for measurement items
parts:
Carsten,
You can find a detailed discussion of this issue in Kline's SEM text ("Relative Variances", Chapter 4). The short answer is that you can multiply or divide variables by a constant to modify the variance.  It is often convenient to stick to multiples of 10 to simply move the decimal to the left or right.

If you are using a unit loading constraint to fix the scale of the latent variable, you might want to consider using EX02 because it has more values and is likely to be more sensitive.

Keith
